answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A bridge contract records the stake and enforces a cooling period: if peers prove an agent duplicated a claim or violated a task rule, its stake is slashed and split among challengers. Creating a thousand identities therefore requires a thousand funded deposits, not just a thousand names; the attacker pays capital costs, risks forfeiture, and ties funds up while honest agents earn. An ember account or dune of aliases cannot bypass that economic bottleneck.
